changesets.summary: Edit, schedule and cancel social drafts from agents.
Authenticate analytics account claims and reserve product actions for server capture
Apply analytics request ceilings before parsing, path lookup and replay processing, including rejected requests.
Read today’s date in the calendar in dark mode
changesets.details: The highlighted date uses dark text on its bright background in either theme.

changesets.summary: Prevent login servers from executing commands through the Windows browser launcher; restrict sign-in links to the configured site's approval page.
Describe the longer edit window in the CLI
changesets.details: `slopper edit` now says editing stays open until the end of the day after launch, at least 24 hours after launch, matching the server's `editableUntil`.

changesets.summary: Launch a PDF or EPUB you wrote from the CLI
changesets.details: `--publication ./guide.pdf` (or `./zine.epub`) on `slopper launch` uploads a book, zine, guide or paper (up to 4 MB) to read from the slop page, and makes `--link` optional. On `slopper edit` it swaps the file, and `--remove-publication` takes it off.

changesets.summary: Add repository metadata to published CLI packages
changesets.details: Include the private source repository and package directory in the CLI and skill package manifests so release metadata satisfies monochange 0.21.0. The packages remain closed source and UNLICENSED.

changesets.summary: Group social commands under slopper social, with help for each command.
Per-destination links, media, first comments and times, ideas, and resolving uncertain copies
changesets.details: Adds --link-for, --comment-for, --media-for and --time-for to social post and social edit, allows social post --at draft without accounts, and adds slopper social resolve <delivery> --posted [--link url] | --resend.

changesets.summary: Let agents edit, schedule and cancel social drafts, and document promo video workflows.
Post to your social accounts from the CLI
changesets.details:
`slopper social-accounts` lists the accounts you can post as. `slopper social-post "<text>" --account <id> ...` sends one
post to all of them, each copy fitted to its network, with `--thread`, `--first-comment`, `--link`, `--image`,
`--tag`, `--track-links` and `--at now|queue|draft|<date-time>`. `--key` makes retries safe: the same key returns the
same post. `slopper social-posts` and `slopper social-status <post>` show where each copy went and how it's doing.
The skill explains when to use them.

changesets.summary: Bind saved CLI tokens to their saved origin and require HTTPS outside loopback development
Comments are back, checked and moderated
changesets.details: Every slop page takes feedback and kudos again. A new comment passes the content check: blocked words are refused, and anything mature or unchecked waits for a moderator before it appears. People can flag comments, and enough flags hide one until a moderator decides. Approve someone's comment once and they are trusted: their later comments skip the check and the hourly cap.

changesets.summary: Enforce the disabled comments feature in public Convex page queries
Edit a launch through the next day
changesets.details: A launch's original post now stays editable until the end of the day after it goes out, at least 24 hours after launch. Previously it closed at the end of the launch day, or 12 hours after a late launch. After the longer window closes, the original post is locked and changes go in updates, as before.

changesets.summary: Validate EPUB manifest media types and spine references before publication uploads, refusing resources that readers could reinterpret as unchecked active content.
Keep confirmations and errors until their page loads
changesets.details: Background requests no longer hide Settings confirmations and errors before you can see them.

changesets.summary: Consume flash cookies only when the page delivers the message
changesets.details: Background resource and child-only data requests leave the message for the root loader.

changesets.summary: Resolve form media only for the signed-in owner and the expected media type.
Bound anonymous hall-of-fame queries
changesets.details: Cap hall-of-fame reads and card expansion at 100 winners. Normalize finite result limits to non-negative integers and reject non-finite limits before database work.

changesets.summary: Drain rejected MCP request bodies before reusing their HTTP connection
Update monochange to 0.20.1
changesets.details: The release tooling moves to `@monochange/cli` 0.20.1, which installs its npm binary with the executable bit set and supports opening release pull requests through monochange.dev.

changesets.summary: Update release tooling to monochange 0.21.0
changesets.details: Use the verified monochange 0.21.0 CLI for configuration, changeset checks and release planning. Preserve all other tool versions and allow only this exact release through the package age gate.

changesets.summary: Reject PDF OpenAction and AA hooks before content checks and storage, including escaped names, indirect actions and compressed objects.
PDF publications can no longer open links automatically. Clicked links still work. PDFs with automatic hooks, including opening-view settings, need to be exported again as plain PDFs.
Inspect unfiltered PDF object streams and every filter stage before accepting publications; reject ambiguous headers and incomplete decoding.
Hold new and edited launches until a current moderation verdict; retain scheduled completion retries.
Keep scheduled launch dates and counts private to you until they go live.
Launches and edits stay private while their content check is unavailable. Scheduled launches retry failed checks.
Bound publication upload attempts before parsing
changesets.details: Limit browser body reads by account and address. Charge malformed and rejected publications against the upload budget before safety scans or decompression.

changesets.summary: Publications (PDFs and EPUBs) on slops
changesets.details:
- `slops.publication` and `scheduledLaunches.publication` hold one PDF's media id; media rows keep a `fileName`. `PublicSlop.publication` is `{ url, fileName, size }` or null, and cards show "PDF" beside the platforms.
- `scanPdf` (app/.server/pdfSafety.ts) is a pdfid-style safety scan run before anything else: it undoes `#xx` name escapes, inflates object streams (capped at `MAX_INFLATED_BYTES` against bombs), skips stream data only where `/Length` lands on `endstream`, and refuses polyglots, encryption, active content (`/JavaScript`, `/Launch`, `/SubmitForm`, `/XFA`, script URIs…), attachments and object streams it can't read. The reason maps to a message in `PDF_PROBLEMS`.
- `scanEpub` (app/.server/epubSafety.ts) is the EPUB side: it reads the ZIP's directory and requires its entries to sit end to end with nothing around them, unpacks each (capped at `MAX_UNPACKED_BYTES`) and checks its size and CRC, refuses climbing or twin names, ZIP64, encrypted entries and DRM (font obfuscation is fine), only lets in the files a book is made of, and reads every page, drawing and stylesheet with a quote-aware tag reader: scripts, frames, forms, `on*` handlers, code URLs (after undoing character references and CSS escapes) and anything that loads from the web are refused. It returns the book's text, which the content check reads as a text part instead of a file part. `EPUB_PROBLEMS` holds the messages.
- Publications are `PUBLICATION_TYPES.pdf` or `.epub` (`publicationFormat` in convex/lib/media.ts), stored under `publications/` with their own extension; `PublicPublication` and the form's publication carry `format`, and upload results return it.
- `uploadPublication` (app/.server/media.ts) sniffs an EPUB's leading `mimetype` entry or `%PDF-`, caps at `LIMITS.publicationBytes`, runs `scanPdf`, and runs the content check with the PDF inline as a `file` part and OpenRouter's free `pdf-text` parser. Blocked ones are refused, mature ones blur the slop through `checkScreenshots`, and an unchecked one is sent again with the launch check.
- `validateSlop` takes a link or a publication. Screenshots only take images now (`isImage`), and `releaseMedia` counts publications as shown.
- Agents: the `upload_publication` operation, `POST /api/v1/publications` (raw PDF with `?fileName=`, or JSON), and `publication` on `create_slop`/`update_slop` (null takes it off).

changesets.summary: Upload your own publication
changesets.details: Wrote a book, zine, guide or paper? Launch it as a slop: upload the PDF or EPUB (up to 4 MB) and people read it straight from the slop page. With one, links are optional. Every file goes through Slopper's own safety scan first, so nobody who opens one gets scripts, auto-run actions, hidden attachments, trackers that load from the web or a file disguised as a book. Then it's checked like a screenshot, and agents can upload one too.

changesets.summary: Stop rate-limit cleanup from rescheduling on pages of live rows while continuing to drain expired rows.
Hydrate launch ages from the serialized page clock and format calendar fallbacks in UTC.
Bound replay decompression, JSON allocations and event counts during playback
Keep owner launch, goal and integration pages out of session replay, including encoded route names.
Charge the review budget before content checks, including blocked and failed attempts.
Screenshots and videos open full screen
changesets.details: Open screenshots, update images and review images in a full-screen gallery without leaving the page. Use the arrows to browse, and Escape or Close to return. Promo videos have a button to open the same view.

changesets.summary: Bound signed-in search work and embedding spend with one account quota across browser, REST and MCP
Harden ingestion limits and security checks
changesets.details:
Round one — the attacks the audits proved, closed:

- Analytics ingestion (`/a/e`, `/a/r`) is public, so it now has ceilings: events per minute and per UTC day, per distinct id, merges into an account, and recording bytes and chunks (packages/analytics). A flood hits the ceiling — and the shared counter slows it down — instead of the deployment's storage and function budget; honest traffic never notices.
- Share-card URLs only render their canonical version: any other `?v=` is redirected to it (301), so made-up query strings can't fill the CDN or make the server draw. Drawing also reads a new, lighter `slops.card` query, and each address has an hourly ceiling.
- Anonymous routes that cost a Convex write per request are rate limited per address: OAuth starts (30/h), CLI polls (720/h), scheduled-launch claims (600/h, id-shaped first), unsubscribes (60/h), REST and MCP pre-limits (4800/h) before a bearer is resolved, and the MCP endpoint refuses requests without a token before parsing their body (draining it, so keep-alive connections survive). Anonymous wall searches get the API's 120/h too: each one costs an embedding model call.
- Editing a slop is limited (30/day) and clears its content-check verdict the moment the checked content changes: a re-check that errors leaves it held for a moderator, the way a launch that fails its check is, instead of showing a stale "ok" over new text.
- Public queries are bounded: a day's race caps at 500 items, goal standings at 2,000 goals × 2,000 slops, a slop's page at 500 updates/comments/launches.
- Upvotes notify their owner once an hour per slop, not once per toggle; avatar copies from providers time out after 10s and refuse oversized bodies.

Round two — deeper audits, all fixed:

- A check verdict now carries a fingerprint of the content it judged (`moderation.applyCheck`): a check that was in flight while the slop was edited lands on nothing, so swapped-in text can never ride an "ok" out to the maker's social accounts.
- Scheduled releases the app server never finished (it was down, or `tellApp` gave up) are retried by a 15-minute cron backstop, so a launch can't sit live and unchecked.
- Deleting a slop no longer refunds its voters' five votes for the day.
- `money.add` and `goals.create` validate their numbers Convex-side (NaN, negatives and degenerate goals are refused, not stored).
- `safeReturnTo` rejects control characters: a tab after the slash turned `/\t//evil.com` into a redirect off the site after login.
- The CSP is nonce-based — no more `unsafe-inline` scripts — and static files get `nosniff` and the referrer policy at the edge too. The two preference cookies are `Secure` on HTTPS.
- Every outbound fetch to an address a person typed (a Bluesky PDS, self-hosted PostHog, the Solana RPC, a slop's website) rides the SSRF-pinned transport, which checks the address inside the DNS lookup it connects with: DNS rebinding can't slip a private address past.
- `media.url` (any media id → its URL) is server-only; API tokens expire after a year; uploads nothing ever attaches to are swept after two weeks; the OAuth-state/session/rate-limit sweeper reschedules itself while there's more, so floods can't outgrow it; and the fflate copy satori pulls in is pinned past its CVE.

Pinned so they can't quietly come back: `tests/security.test.ts` (every public Convex function names an auth gate; the CSP keeps its nonce; the one raw-HTML sink stays the sanitizer; anonymous Convex-costing routes keep a ceiling; ingest caps stay caps), `tests/replay-sandbox.test.ts` (the replay iframe never allows scripts), and `e2e/security.spec.ts` (the exploits themselves, replayed every CI run).

changesets.summary: Canonicalize the complete share-card URL before fetching media or rendering to prevent cache-busting requests from triggering duplicate work.
The skill knows "deploy this to Slopper" means launch a slop
changesets.details: Its description now triggers on asking to deploy, ship or post a project to Slopper, and it says that means launching the project as a slop that links to where it already runs.

changesets.summary: The skill launches publications with --publication
See a larger, network-specific preview for each social account, with playable videos and image carousels.
Take the Solana Hacker House challenge November 1–12, with three shipping targets and a launch tag.
Launch ages stay consistent while pages open, even across time boundaries and time zones.
Add the studio's posting engine, network adapters and agent access
changesets.details:
- `socialPosts` and `socialDeliveries` in Convex (`convex/social.ts`): one leased delivery per account, with
  staggering (`notBefore`), reposts that wait for an original, repeats, pause, idempotency keys, a duplicate guard,
  an activity log, and a backstop that marks lost sends uncertain instead of resending them.
- Supporting tables in `convex/studio.ts`: settings (queue slots, pause, calendar token, webhook), snippets, brand
  voices, tracked links, preview links and RSS feeds.
- Network adapters gain `reply`, `remove` and `comments`, alt text, covers, collaborators, LinkedIn documents and
  YouTube thumbnails. One table, `app/lib/networks.ts`, says what each network takes.
- New routes: `/studio/calendar`, `/studio/settings`, `/studio/analytics.csv`, `/review/:token`, `/go/:code`,
  `/api/studio/assist`, `/api/studio/calendar/:token`, `/api/social/feeds`.
- Agent operations `list_social_accounts`, `create_social_post`, `list_social_posts` and `get_social_post` (MCP and
  `/api/v1/social/*`), with CLI commands `social-accounts`, `social-post`, `social-posts` and `social-status`.
- OAuth connect scopes for comments, replies and deletion on Meta and Threads.

changesets.summary: Shared destination resolution and readiness for the studio
changesets.details:
- `app/lib/destinations.ts`: `destinationFor` (account, then network, then shared), `readiness` (block/warn/info issues), `xTwins`, X prices. Used by the composer, `saveStudioPost` and the agent operations; a `block` is refused on save.
- `socialPosts.variants` (media subset, link, first comment per network or account) and `socialPosts.times` (account id to time, setting `notBefore`); drafts may have no accounts; `socialSettings.lastAccountIds`.
- `social.resolveUncertain`, the `resolve_social_delivery` operation and `POST /api/v1/social/deliveries/:delivery/resolve`; `retry` skips uncertain deliveries.
- `wallTime` is DST-safe; the composer reads typed times in the profile time zone.
- Mastodon media uploads go through the pinned transport.
- Reddit OAuth (`REDDIT_CLIENT_*`) with refreshing tokens and subreddits per account; LinkedIn Pages behind `LINKEDIN_PAGES` (Community Management API scopes, `organizationAcls`).
- `app/lib/setupGuides.ts` and docs/social-setup.md: setup steps for every network.

changesets.summary: Post to every account without surprises
changesets.details:
- A checklist for each account says whether it's ready ("Instagram needs a picture or a video") with a button that takes you to the fix.
- Give a network or one account its own link, pictures and first comment, and go back to the shared version in one click.
- Send at the same time everywhere or pick a time per account. Times are read in your profile's time zone, across clock changes, and the composer says which.
- "Last used" and "Post as <product>" pick a set of accounts in one tap.
- Save ideas before choosing any accounts. What you're writing is kept in your browser and offered back if you leave.
- Two X accounts can't post the same words (X's rules), and each X post shows what X will bill your app.
- A post that may or may not have gone out is never sent again on its own: check the network, then tell Slopper it posted or send it again.
- Settings → Accounts shows whether each account is connected, expiring soon or needs reconnecting, and a step-by-step guide for setting up every network.
- Reddit connects with your Reddit account, and each subreddit you add is its own destination. LinkedIn Company Pages can be connected once LinkedIn approves the app.
- Best-time suggestions are per account and labelled as estimates; previews are labelled as approximations.

changesets.summary: The studio: write one post and send it to all your accounts at once
changesets.details:
Write once in the studio and post it to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Threads, Facebook Pages, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube,
as whichever brand it's for. Each network gets a copy that fits it, and you see how it will look before it goes out.

- Threads, a first comment, alt text, LinkedIn PDF documents, video covers and YouTube thumbnails.
- Drafts, editing, a weekly posting queue, the best times to post from your own results, repeating posts, staggered
  accounts, a pause button and bulk scheduling from a spreadsheet.
- A calendar with drag to reschedule, filters, an Instagram grid and a feed for your calendar app.
- Preview links that a client or teammate opens without an account to approve or ask for changes.
- Snippets (hashtag groups, signatures, templates, saved replies), variables and spintax, and a writing assistant that
  follows each brand's voice.
- Comments and replies, taking posts down, reposts by your other accounts, an auto-plug reply once a post takes off,
  and alerts when an account needs reconnecting.
- Analytics by network, account, format and hashtag, tracked links that count clicks per network, and a CSV export.
- Posts from RSS feeds, and signed webhooks for Zapier, Make or your own code.

changesets.summary: Limit traction refresh requests per address before querying slops or claiming integration syncs.
Add second factors and step-up confirmation to sign-in
changesets.details:
- `convex/security.ts`: TOTP factors (sealed secrets, each 30-second step usable once), passkeys (WebAuthn via
  `@simplewebauthn/server`, counter regression refused), hashed one-time recovery codes, short-lived `authChallenges`
  (five tries each, ten per person per 15 minutes) and a per-user `securityEvents` log.
- `app/.server/auth/twoFactor.ts`: `secondFactorGate` holds the session after OAuth until `/login/verify` passes;
  `requireRecentAuth` sends sensitive actions to confirm when the session's `verifiedAt` is over 15 minutes old.
- Sessions record `verifiedAt` and the browser, are indexed by user, and can be ended from `/settings/security`.

changesets.summary: Two-step sign-in with passkeys or an authenticator app
changesets.details:
Turn it on in Settings → Security. Add a passkey (your fingerprint, face, device PIN or a security key) or an
authenticator app, and signing in asks for it after GitHub, Google, X, LinkedIn or Facebook, so a stolen login for one
of those isn't enough to get into your account and every brand it posts as. You get ten recovery codes in case you
lose your phone. Making API tokens, approving the CLI, connecting accounts, and setting up webhooks and feeds ask you to
confirm it's you again after 15 minutes. The security page also lists where you're signed in, signs out other
browsers, and keeps a log of sign-ins and changes.

changesets.summary: Reserve update quota before fetching link previews and retain charges for failed attempts
Connect multiple X brand accounts using your own developer app credentials and API credits. Choose which accounts post for each product.

Anonymous wall searches get the API's 120/h too: each one costs an embedding model call.
- Editing a slop is limited (30/day) and clears its content-check verdict the moment the checked content changes: a re-check that errors leaves it held for a moderator, the way a launch that fails its check is, instead of showing a stale "ok" over new text.
- Public queries are bounded: a day's race caps at 500 items, goal standings at 2,000 goals × 2,000 slops, a slop's page at 500 updates/comments/launches.

- A check verdict now carries a fingerprint of the content it judged (`moderation.applyCheck`): a check that was in flight while the slop was edited lands on nothing, so swapped-in text can never ride an "ok" out to the maker's social accounts.
- Scheduled releases the app server never finished (it was down, or `tellApp` gave up) are retried by a 15-minute cron backstop, so a launch can't sit live and unchecked.
- Deleting a slop no longer refunds its voters' five votes for the day.
- `money.add` and `goals.create` validate their numbers Convex-side (NaN, negatives and degenerate goals are refused, not stored).
- `safeReturnTo` rejects control characters: a tab after the slash turned `/\t//evil.com` into a redirect off the site after login.
- The CSP is nonce-based — no more `unsafe-inline` scripts — and static files get `nosniff` and the referrer policy at the edge too. The two preference cookies are `Secure` on HTTPS.
- Every outbound fetch to an address a person typed (a Bluesky PDS, self-hosted PostHog, the Solana RPC, a slop's website) rides the SSRF-pinned transport, which checks the address inside the DNS lookup it connects with: DNS rebinding can't slip a private address past.

## 1.12.0 (2026-11-04)

### Features

#### Publications (PDFs and EPUBs) on slops

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ aa17b4c

- `slops.publication` and `scheduledLaunches.publication` hold one PDF's media id; media rows keep a `fileName`. `PublicSlop.publication` is `{ url, fileName, size }` or null, and cards show "PDF" beside the platforms.
- `scanPdf` (app/.server/pdfSafety.ts) is a pdfid-style safety scan run before anything else: it undoes `#xx` name escapes, inflates object streams (capped at `MAX_INFLATED_BYTES` against bombs), skips stream data only where `/Length` lands on `endstream`, and refuses polyglots, encryption, active content (`/JavaScript`, `/Launch`, `/SubmitForm`, `/XFA`, script URIs…), attachments and object streams it can't read. The reason maps to a message in `PDF_PROBLEMS`.
- `scanEpub` (app/.server/epubSafety.ts) is the EPUB side: it reads the ZIP's directory and requires its entries to sit end to end with nothing around them, unpacks each (capped at `MAX_UNPACKED_BYTES`) and checks its size and CRC, refuses climbing or twin names, ZIP64, encrypted entries and DRM (font obfuscation is fine), only lets in the files a book is made of, and reads every page, drawing and stylesheet with a quote-aware tag reader: scripts, frames, forms, `on*` handlers, code URLs (after undoing character references and CSS escapes) and anything that loads from the web are refused. It returns the book's text, which the content check reads as a text part instead of a file part. `EPUB_PROBLEMS` holds the messages.
- Publications are `PUBLICATION_TYPES.pdf` or `.epub` (`publicationFormat` in convex/lib/media.ts), stored under `publications/` with their own extension; `PublicPublication` and the form's publication carry `format`, and upload results return it.
- `uploadPublication` (app/.server/media.ts) sniffs an EPUB's leading `mimetype` entry or `%PDF-`, caps at `LIMITS.publicationBytes`, runs `scanPdf`, and runs the content check with the PDF inline as a `file` part and OpenRouter's free `pdf-text` parser. Blocked ones are refused, mature ones blur the slop through `checkScreenshots`, and an unchecked one is sent again with the launch check.
- `validateSlop` takes a link or a publication. Screenshots only take images now (`isImage`), and `releaseMedia` counts publications as shown.
- Agents: the `upload_publication` operation, `POST /api/v1/publications` (raw PDF with `?fileName=`, or JSON), and `publication` on `create_slop`/`update_slop` (null takes it off).

#### Add the studio's posting engine, network adapters and agent access

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ a600d8e

- `socialPosts` and `socialDeliveries` in Convex (`convex/social.ts`): one leased delivery per account, with
  staggering (`notBefore`), reposts that wait for an original, repeats, pause, idempotency keys, a duplicate guard,
  an activity log, and a backstop that marks lost sends uncertain instead of resending them.
- Supporting tables in `convex/studio.ts`: settings (queue slots, pause, calendar token, webhook), snippets, brand
  voices, tracked links, preview links and RSS feeds.
- Network adapters gain `reply`, `remove` and `comments`, alt text, covers, collaborators, LinkedIn documents and
  YouTube thumbnails. One table, `app/lib/networks.ts`, says what each network takes.
- New routes: `/studio/calendar`, `/studio/settings`, `/studio/analytics.csv`, `/review/:token`, `/go/:code`,
  `/api/studio/assist`, `/api/studio/calendar/:token`, `/api/social/feeds`.
- Agent operations `list_social_accounts`, `create_social_post`, `list_social_posts` and `get_social_post` (MCP and
  `/api/v1/social/*`), with CLI commands `social-accounts`, `social-post`, `social-posts` and `social-status`.
- OAuth connect scopes for comments, replies and deletion on Meta and Threads.

#### Shared destination resolution and readiness for the studio

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

- `app/lib/destinations.ts`: `destinationFor` (account, then network, then shared), `readiness` (block/warn/info issues), `xTwins`, X prices. Used by the composer, `saveStudioPost` and the agent operations; a `block` is refused on save.

- Mastodon media uploads go through the pinned transport.

- `app/lib/setupGuides.ts` and docs/social-setup.md: setup steps for every network.

#### Add second factors and step-up confirmation to sign-in

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ f70714e

sections.title: New
entries:
- **Edit, schedule and cancel social drafts from agents.**
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

- **Comments are back, checked and moderated.** Every slop page takes feedback and kudos again. A new comment passes the content check: blocked words are refused, and anything mature or unchecked waits for a moderator before it appears. People can flag comments, and enough flags hide one until a moderator decides. Approve someone's comment once and they are trusted: their later comments skip the check and the hourly cap.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 3871f2d

- **Edit a launch through the next day.** A launch's original post now stays editable until the end of the day after it goes out, at least 24 hours after launch. Previously it closed at the end of the launch day, or 12 hours after a late launch. After the longer window closes, the original post is locked and changes go in updates, as before.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 7486bdb

- **Upload your own publication.** Wrote a book, zine, guide or paper? Launch it as a slop: upload the PDF or EPUB (up to 4 MB) and people read it straight from the slop page. With one, links are optional. Every file goes through Slopper's own safety scan first, so nobody who opens one gets scripts, auto-run actions, hidden attachments, trackers that load from the web or a file disguised as a book. Then it's checked like a screenshot, and agents can upload one too.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ aa17b4c

- **See a larger, network-specific preview for each social account, with playable videos and image carousels.**
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

- **Take the Solana Hacker House challenge November 1–12, with three shipping targets and a launch tag.**
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ dc05cb0

#### Post to every account without surprises

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

- A checklist for each account says whether it's ready ("Instagram needs a picture or a video") with a button that takes you to the fix.
- Give a network or one account its own link, pictures and first comment, and go back to the shared version in one click.
- Send at the same time everywhere or pick a time per account. Times are read in your profile's time zone, across clock changes, and the composer says which.
- "Last used" and "Post as <product>" pick a set of accounts in one tap.
- Save ideas before choosing any accounts. What you're writing is kept in your browser and offered back if you leave.
- Two X accounts can't post the same words (X's rules), and each X post shows what X will bill your app.
- A post that may or may not have gone out is never sent again on its own: check the network, then tell Slopper it posted or send it again.
- Settings → Accounts shows whether each account is connected, expiring soon or needs reconnecting, and a step-by-step guide for setting up every network.
- Reddit connects with your Reddit account, and each subreddit you add is its own destination. LinkedIn Company Pages can be connected once LinkedIn approves the app.
- Best-time suggestions are per account and labelled as estimates; previews are labelled as approximations.

#### The studio: write one post and send it to all your accounts at once

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ a600d8e

Write once in the studio and post it to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Threads, Facebook Pages, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube,
as whichever brand it's for. Each network gets a copy that fits it, and you see how it will look before it goes out.

- Threads, a first comment, alt text, LinkedIn PDF documents, video covers and YouTube thumbnails.
- Drafts, editing, a weekly posting queue, the best times to post from your own results, repeating posts, staggered
  accounts, a pause button and bulk scheduling from a spreadsheet.
- A calendar with drag to reschedule, filters, an Instagram grid and a feed for your calendar app.
- Preview links that a client or teammate opens without an account to approve or ask for changes.
- Snippets (hashtag groups, signatures, templates, saved replies), variables and spintax, and a writing assistant that
  follows each brand's voice.
- Comments and replies, taking posts down, reposts by your other accounts, an auto-plug reply once a post takes off,
  and alerts when an account needs reconnecting.
- Analytics by network, account, format and hashtag, tracked links that count clicks per network, and a CSV export.
- Posts from RSS feeds, and signed webhooks for Zapier, Make or your own code.

#### Two-step sign-in with passkeys or an authenticator app

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ f70714e

Turn it on in Settings → Security. Add a passkey (your fingerprint, face, device PIN or a security key) or an
authenticator app, and signing in asks for it after GitHub, Google, X, LinkedIn or Facebook, so a stolen login for one
of those isn't enough to get into your account and every brand it posts as. You get ten recovery codes in case you
lose your phone. Making API tokens, approving the CLI, connecting accounts, and setting up webhooks and feeds ask you to
confirm it's you again after 15 minutes. The security page also lists where you're signed in, signs out other
browsers, and keeps a log of sign-ins and changes.

- **Connect multiple X brand accounts using your own developer app credentials and API credits.** Choose which accounts post for each product.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ a600d8e

entries:

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 7e3b6f2

- **Keep confirmations and errors until their page loads.** Background requests no longer hide Settings confirmations and errors before you can see them.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 36551a5

  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 5e57c09

- **Screenshots and videos open full screen.** Open screenshots, update images and review images in a full-screen gallery without leaving the page. Use the arrows to browse, and Escape or Close to return. Promo videos have a button to open the same view.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 7e3b6f2

entries:
- **Launch a PDF or EPUB you wrote from the CLI.** `--publication ./guide.pdf` (or `./zine.epub`) on `slopper launch` uploads a book, zine, guide or paper (up to 4 MB) to read from the slop page, and makes `--link` optional. On `slopper edit` it swaps the file, and `--remove-publication` takes it off.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ aa17b4c

- **Group social commands under slopper social, with help for each command.**
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

- **Per-destination links, media, first comments and times, ideas, and resolving uncertain copies.** Adds --link-for, --comment-for, --media-for and --time-for to social post and social edit, allows social post --at draft without accounts, and adds slopper social resolve <delivery> --posted [--link url] | --resend.
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

- **Let agents edit, schedule and cancel social drafts, and document promo video workflows.**
  _Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 43dfb42

#### Post to your social accounts from the CLI

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ a600d8e

`slopper social-accounts` lists the accounts you can post as. `slopper social-post "<text>" --account <id> ...` sends one
post to all of them, each copy fitted to its network, with `--thread`, `--first-comment`, `--link`, `--image`,
`--tag`, `--track-links` and `--at now|queue|draft|<date-time>`. `--key` makes retries safe: the same key returns the
same post. `slopper social-posts` and `slopper social-status <post>` show where each copy went and how it's doing.
The skill explains when to use them.

#### Post to your social accounts from the CLI

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ a600d8e

`slopper social-accounts` lists the accounts you can post as. `slopper social-post "<text>" --account <id> ...` sends one
post to all of them, each copy fitted to its network, with `--thread`, `--first-comment`, `--link`, `--image`,
`--tag`, `--track-links` and `--at now|queue|draft|<date-time>`. `--key` makes retries safe: the same key returns the
same post. `slopper social-posts` and `slopper social-status <post>` show where each copy went and how it's doing.
The skill explains when to use them.
